gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-m-plus-1: Happy Monkey draws its lines ruler-straight, with wide gaps in every e, and it announces itself loudly. M PLUS 1 sits beneath in sans-serif form, its big open eyes giving the loudness somewhere quiet to land.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-m-plus-1p: Blunt, cheerful, and uniform in its stroke, Happy Monkey leads with wide gaps in the e. And M PLUS 1p follows as a plain sans whose curve ends stay open, which is the pair's real strength.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-m-plus-2: Happy Monkey's ruler-straight lines make it unmistakable. M PLUS 2 follows as a plain sans with a gaping c and one fixed nib width, and the heading earns its keep when it runs big and brief.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-m-plus-code-latin: M PLUS Code Latin bends its letters like neon tubing, each c a wide pitcher mouth, while Happy Monkey shouts bold above it. And a long read in that sans would feel friendly and uncluttered, with no line fighting another.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-m-plus-rounded-1c: Happy Monkey has no calligraphic swelling anywhere in its outlines, just ruler-straight strokes and wide gaps in the e. M PLUS Rounded 1c is the sans-serif partner whose terminals stop short of curling back, so the page reads as one friendly, plain-spoken voice.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-mandali: Happy Monkey builds its capitals from lines of one constant thickness. Mandali, a sans with a generous entry into the e's eye, brings a gentler, more approachable ease, and that softness against the heading's boldness is the pair's best quality.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-manjari: Happy Monkey's ruler-straight lines and wide-gapped e give it a bold, distinctive face. And Manjari, the sans-serif below, does the quieter job well, with unclosed curve ends and a steady line that carry text smoothly.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-meera-inimai: Happy Monkey stands out first for its ruler-straight line weight and wide-gapped e, a loud display voice. Meera Inimai handles the steady work, a sans of open-ended curves with a blueprint-lettering feel that gives text room to breathe.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-metrophobic: Metrophobic is a modern sans that lets the eye glide around each bend. Happy Monkey above it presses strokes like twine into a flat surface, and that handmade bluntness against the smooth text is what makes the pair memorable.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-mingzat: Mingzat reads curvy and unclamped, a contemporary sans-serif that never feels stiff. Happy Monkey, tracing what feels like a single thick thread, is the one to grab attention, while Mingzat is the one to hold it through the text.
